summary: SIEM feed s125_double is degraded by 14.7% duplicate packets (392/2673); 66.7% one-way TCP sessions (142/213) also detected but tolerable for this SIEM which does not require bidirectional flows.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering the same packets twice, typically from overlapping SPAN/mirror sessions or dual TAP feeds aggregated without deduplication enabled.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM wastes EPS, license and storage on duplicates, inflates event counts and can skew correlation/analytics without improving detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop the 14.7% duplicates before delivery while preserving one correct copy for the SIEM.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of TCP sessions reaches the tool, likely due to asymmetric routing with single-sided SPAN/TAP or broker not aggregating both directions to the same egress port.
findings.impact_on_tool: Low impact for this SIEM (needs_both_directions=false) which can operate on single-direction metadata/flows; no major detection loss for SIEM use case, but indicates incomplete bidirectional visibility if feed is reused for NDR/IDS.

recommended_fix.why: No broker change required for SIEM as configured; if bidirectional analysis is later needed, use aggregate to ensure both directions of each flow are delivered to the same tool port.
